title: Finite Q3 Kubo-Mori energy-moment transfer and QFT interface
question: Can the finite Kubo-Mori spectral second moment be transferred to an explicit shifted Gibbs energy moment on the actual Q3 histories, and which additional hypothesis is required before this can serve as a QFT common-core estimate?
method: Use the registered edge, square, and six-site 2x3 Q3 Hamiltonians with oscillator dimension three, the observable supported on sites 0,1, beta in {0.5,1,2}, radius 0.5, time 0.05, and both cutoff orientations.
Diagonalize each actual finite Hamiltonian, form Gibbs probabilities p_i and logarithmic-mean weights L(p_i,p_j), and shift the spectrum by its actual minimum plus one so k_i>=1.
Evaluate S=2 sum_ij L(p_i,p_j)((E_i-E_j)/hbar)^2 |D_hat_ij|^2 for each actual Q3 history and verify the arithmetic-mean and square-gap inequalities row by row.
Run independent primary and eigenbasis lanes and compile Lean R313 for the exact rational gap, mean-weight transfer, constant, and shifted-energy fixtures.
finding: Primary 115/115, independent 103/103, integrated 13/13, and Lean R313 PASS over 18 actual rows. The safe finite-dimensional Hilbert-Schmidt transfer S <= 8 M2 ||D||_HS^2 holds in every row. The sharper operator-norm candidate S <= 8 M2 ||D||_operator^2 also passes all declared rows, with the largest observed ratio S/(M2||D||_operator^2)=3.4553020779615164; this is an empirical row result, not a general operator-norm theorem. The shifted Gibbs moment M2 is finite in every row and ranges from 1.9205583860609077 to 33.286943994754964 across the declared beta-volume grid. The largest safe Hilbert-Schmidt ratio is 0.38662982758364417. The minimum square-gap slack is 4.0 up to floating-point roundoff and the minimum logarithmic-mean slack is no smaller than -1.554481482245992e-17. None of these finite values supplies a source-, volume-, beta-, cutoff-, or exhaustion-uniform local M2 estimate.
decision_reason: The finite Q3 spectral moment now has a reusable energy-moment interface: the arithmetic-mean logarithmic-mean bound and shifted square-gap inequality give a rigorous finite Hilbert-Schmidt estimate, and the actual operator-norm candidate survives all 18 histories. The hostile review prevents promotion of that candidate to a general theorem because the aggregate cross terms do not follow from operator norm alone without an additional structural argument. The remaining QFT target is therefore explicit: establish a local/source/volume/beta-uniform M2 and common-core D estimate (or prove a valid operator-norm replacement) before attempting common alpha, modular transfer, OS/KMS/GNS identification, or any gap/continuum claim.
closed: finite shifted-energy Gibbs moment and arithmetic-mean transfer fixtures
finite Hilbert-Schmidt transfer bound on actual edge, square, and six-site Q3 rows
actual two-orientation history rows at beta 0.5,1,2
independent reproduction and Lean R313 cross-check
open: general operator-norm transfer theorem or a replacement structural bound
source-, volume-, beta-, cutoff-, and exhaustion-uniform local M2 estimate
high-energy/common-core tail control and modular-domain transfer
broken-sector gap, continuum, C6, Sector A and Pre-A

adversarial_review.check: Every finite spectrum is shifted by its actual minimum plus the declared positive constant; all square-gap calculations use shift-invariant differences and nonnegative k_i.
The equal-probability limit is explicit and the arithmetic-mean upper bound is checked on every actual Gibbs spectrum.
The rigorous finite transfer retained by the checkpoint uses the Hilbert-Schmidt norm; no Hilbert-Schmidt-to-operator-norm replacement is silently made.
The sharper operator-norm expression passes the declared rows, but aggregate cross terms are not promoted without an additional theorem controlling their Gibbs-weighted orientation.
M2 is a global finite Gibbs moment in each row; the finite range is not a local or volume-uniform common-core estimate.
Direct Cauchy, common core, exhaustion, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A, and Pre-A remain open.

qft_interface.closed: A finite conditional interface from the Kubo-Mori derivative spectral moment to a shifted Gibbs energy moment, with a rigorous Hilbert-Schmidt finite bound and a separately labelled operator-norm candidate.
qft_interface.open: Uniform local/common-core energy control, a general operator-norm replacement if needed, modular-domain transfer, product/core density, exhaustion independence, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS identification, gap, continuum and Pre-A.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: The factor-eight finite estimate identifies the analytic quantity that must be controlled before QFT promotion; it is not a thermodynamic limit or a Clay proof.

next_action: Prove or refute a source/volume/beta-uniform local M2 and high-energy tail estimate for the actual Q3 D history on a declared unbounded common core. If the operator-norm candidate is needed, supply an independent structural argument for its aggregate cross terms; otherwise carry the Hilbert-Schmidt norm through the direct Cauchy route and quantify the dimension dependence.
boundary: This is a finite actual-Q3 energy-moment audit over three graph volumes, three beta values, one cutoff, one time, and both orientations. It is not a uniform common-core theorem, an infinite-volume dynamics, a QFT reconstruction, a gap, continuum, C6, Sector A, or Pre-A result.
no_overclaim: The finite Hilbert-Schmidt transfer is exact within the declared finite spectral setting. The operator-norm version is an empirical candidate only. The checkpoint does not prove a uniform local energy moment, direct D/delta-D Cauchy, common alpha, Sector A, Pre-A, or any Clay statement.
